text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Thursday.

GERMANY - German Bunds closed slightly firmer on Thursday after being knocked off their session highs by the news that Russian President Boris Yeltsin sacked his security chief, Alexander Lebed. Reports of political instability in Russia had weighed on the market all day but Bunds had managed to chalk up modest gains in response to firming U.S. Treasuries. The December Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 99.27, up 0.03 from Wednesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - UK gilts held their ground on Thursday in a nervous market, underpinned by the relentless rise in sterling. There was little reaction to Russian President Boris Yeltsin's decision to sack his security chief Alexander Lebed, despite a small sell-off in Bund futures. The December long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 109-26/32, up 4/32 from Wednesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond futures finished stronger but off their highs in moderate volume on Thursday after Russian President Boris Yeltsin fired Alexander Lebed, his security chief. PIBOR futures and the franc benefitted from the news, as German assets weakened. The dollar traded sharply higher, which also lifted the franc. The December notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 126.00, up 0.16 from Wednesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian debt instruments staged a late recovery after a roller-coaster session and weaker start, helped by firmer U.S. Treasuries on a raft of positive economic data. News that President Yeltsin sacked his security chief Alexander Lebed cast a shadow over German markets and bunds erased earlier gains, but other bond markets gained. The December bond future on LIFFE was trading at 122.16, up 0.29 from Wednesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries were higher in moderate midday trade on Thursday as players returned to the market after a batch of fresh data suggested the economy continues to grow at a slower pace. The December Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 110-28/32, up 18/32 from Wednesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.83 percent.

JAPAN - Key December Japanese government bond futures closed a little higher, after their rebound to 122.55 indicated the firm support they can expect from investors' buying and speculation surrounding the buying. In after hours trading the December future on LIFFE was trading at 122.82, up 0.22 from Wednesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - Fixed-rate dollar deals returned to the frame after a few days' new issuance dominated by European currencies. Toyota Motor Credit Corp set a $500 million five-year deal 11 b.p. over. It quickly moved to a premium on its reoffer level on being freed to trade. Merrill Lynch brought a self-led $150 million three-year. Ford Brazil issued a structured $300 million eight-year. SBC Warburg lead managed a brace of 15-year sterling bonds for Bank Austria and Quebec.
